medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Health Careers Opportunity Program (HCOP) is available for disadvantaged students.

Additional programs include HSTA, MedSTEP, and formal collaborations with WVU undergraduate colleges as well as other local Universities.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request a leave of absence from the standard curriculum for a period of up to one calendar year at any time. All requests are presented and reviewed by the Committee on Academic and Professional Standards (CAPS). CAPs decides as to the terms under which the student may return to the curriculum. Leaves are classified as medical, academic, personal or administrative. Students may be enrolled in an appropriate modified curriculum during the leave of absence depending on the decision of CAPS.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
A WVU SoM student has access to over forty activities, interest groups, and honor societies. These include but are not limited to Golden Key, and specialty interest groups including Military Medicine Interest Group, AMWA, AOA, SNMA, Medical Spanish Association, and WVU soccer. Please see our website for a complete list of the available groups at:

http://medicine.hsc.wvu.edu/md-student-services/organizations/

For a sense of student life in Morgantown, please check out our student services site on Facebook:

https://www.facebook.com/EPylonsWVUMedicalStudents/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The WVU LGBTQ+ Center is a great resource for support for sexual and gender minority students. Several medical student-run organizations, which promote diversity, inclusion, and equity efforts are also active in providing support and education to the WVU community as a whole. The WVU SoM Academy of Advisors includes several outstanding faculty members from varied backgrounds who are available to provide support to sexual and gender minority students who seek mentorship. There are 55+ educational events threaded throughout the MD curriculum to enhance students' care of patients from not only the LGBTQ+ community but from other specialized populations; these educational events also foster a supportive learning environment for all students and faculty.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The West Virginia University Office of Student Accommodations (OSA) assists students in requesting and implementing appropriate accommodations.  If the OSA approves accommodations, the School of Medicine works with faculty to ensure the accommodations are implemented. The West Virginia University School of Medicine also has resources to assist students with disabilities. A learning specialist works with students to detail a study plan and utilize study aids to position students for academic and professional success.  The Peer Assisted Learning Service (PALS) also provides academic resources and peer tutoring.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Several academic support services are available such as PALS, Survive and Thrive – AOA Guide to Med School, and more. A Learning Specialist is readily available for appointments to discuss study strategies, building a consistent study schedule, and more. Health and Mental Health Services are available at each campus.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: WVU fosters an extremely collaborative environment for students and faculty. Kindness, Engagement, Empowerment, and Purpose are the main values emphasized in our campus culture.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: WVU SoM has a Dean-on-Call program. Students may page a student dean for emergencies 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.  PALS is a tutoring service that is available for all students.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Begins during the first week of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: WVU challenges students with a variety of learning experiences including small group problem-solving, simulation-based learning, clinical experiences, and inter-professional learning opportunities.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: During the 3rd and 4th year of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Yes. Students are ranked into quartiles at the end of three years of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: WVU's education provides a strong foundation for any medical specialty. The basic medical sciences are covered primarily in the pre-clerkship phase of the curriculum using a variety of instructional formats, such as didactics, problem-based learning, and simulation-based education. The Physical Diagnosis and Clinical Integration courses integrate the basic and clinical sciences and help students acquire fundamental clinical skills to begin the clerkships. A wide array of summer academic enrichment experiences are available for students between their MS1 and MS2 years. The required MS3 clerkships are medicine, surgery, pediatrics, family medicine, OB-GYN, and psychiatry-neurology. Students may complete  2 weeks of a surgical elective and 2 weeks of a non-surgical elective during the MS3 year. The MS4 year consists of 14 weeks of required and 20 weeks of elective rotations. Two months of rural/community rotations are required.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: WVU SoM requires rural/community rotations with affiliated primary care physicians in West Virginia. WVU SoM is ranked as one of the top 15 schools in rural medicine. Our Rural Scholars Program allows early entry to Family Medicine, Pediatrics, and Internal Medicine. A rural health track is also available to our students.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
WVU is an R1 research institute.
- 8 PhD programs in biomedical and public health sciences
- 4 MS programs including MPH through the School of Public Health
- Interdisciplinary Research Centers and Research Institutes

https://health.wvu.edu/research-and-graduate-education/
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail. Honors designation is limited to no more than the top 15% of a course.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
WVU School of Medicine (SoM) is a public institution located within the Robert C. Byrd Health Sciences Center. The SoM has three campuses: (1) Morgantown, the main campus, was established in 1960 and serves North and Central WV as a primary and tertiary care center; (2) Charleston has served as a regional referral center for Southern WV since 1972; (3) Eastern has provided care to a nine county area in Eastern WV (near MD and VA) since 2002. 
http://medicine.hsc.wvu.edu/students/md-program/
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Improving the health and wellbeing of everyone we serve

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Letters of recommendation should be uploaded into AMCAS at least two weeks prior to your interview. Letters will only be considered when submitted through AMCAS. Additional letters will not increase an applicant's competitiveness.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Applicants must submit either a committee letter from their undergraduate institution or one letter from an individual writer who is able to attest to the applicant's fulfillment of all the core competencies of the AAMC. It is the responsibility of the applicant to share these competencies with their chosen letter writer.

MD/PhD applicants are required to submit an additional letter of recommendation from a Research Principal Investigator/Mentor

medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: When reviewing applications with multiple MCAT scores, the COA looks for an upward trend in scores, with all sub-sections preferably above the 50th percentile. Applicants with multiple MCAT scores with total and/or multiple sub-sections below the 50th percentile will be flagged as potential academic risks and may not be competitive for the cycle in which they apply. Applicants with concerns about recent test scores are encouraged to reach out for academic counseling (pre-med or academic advisor) before attempting an additional MCAT.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: All AMCAS verified applicants will receive a secondary application. Every application is reviewed holistically. Our average MCAT scores for accepted students are available on our website and are indicative of competitive scores for acceptance: https://medicine.hsc.wvu.edu/md-admissions/
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: All AMCAS verified applicants will receive a secondary application. Every application is reviewed holistically. medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo:
A minimum of 90 credit hours (at the undergraduate or graduate level) from an accredited US or Canadian academic institution is required by matriculation. Community college coursework is acceptable.
A minimum of three years of higher education or employment post-high school is required before matriculation.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letter of Intent/Letter of Interest/Notice of Significant Updates must be submitted through our secondary application portal after submission of the secondary application.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: Mountaineer Accelerated Track to Enter Residency (MATTER) is an accelerated pathway toward residency for medical students who have committed to one of 10 participating residency specialties at West Virginia University School of Medicine. Students may apply for MATTER during the second year of the curriculum.  If selected through a competitive process, medical students will complete the M.D. curriculum in 134 weeks, which is 26 weeks shorter than the typical curriculum.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no oldest date. All coursework is acceptable, no matter how long since completion, since we ascribe to competency-based admissions.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The selection process is holistic and has transitioned to being competency-based. WV residents are given the strongest preference as WVU SoM is a land-grant university supported by the state. Well-qualified non-residents, preferably with strong WV ties, are also eligible to apply. Weighted factors include, but are not limited to BCPM GPA, MCAT scores, scholarly accomplishments, patient care/physician shadowing experiences, leadership and educator roles, research, community service/volunteerism, one letter of recommendation, and interview skills. Mastery of AAMC competencies can be demonstrated by a strong performance in the preferred courses and on the MCAT and/or through specialized experiences such as research, employment, military courses, and self-study. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, creed, national origin, age, or disability. Campus assignments for MS3 year are made at the time of acceptance.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing, including in-person and virtual, is just one way that applicants can gain patient care experience. Other roles that may fulfill this mission-based experience requirement include but are not limited to medical scribing, serving as an EMT, nursing, and other medically related positions.
